name: Serpents
overview: Scripture presents serpents as creatures created by God yet cursed because of their role in the fall of man, being doomed to crawl on their belly and eat dust as a consequence of sin (Genesis 3:14). They are characterized by subtlety and danger, exemplified by the serpent's craftiness in the Garden of Eden (Genesis 3:1) and their use as a symbol of enemies and malice (Genesis 49:17). God's power over serpents is demonstrated through miracles such as Moses' rod turning into a serpent, revealing divine authority and judgment (Exodus 4:3; 7:9). The enmity between serpents and humanity ultimately points forward to Christ's victory over evil (Genesis 3:15).
